title: Memory Boundaries: Correction Status
summary: After this intermediate module, a learner can distinguish established correction evidence from UNKNOWN information and identify what is needed to update source-dependent material safely. The learner can also explain why the unavailable baseline prevents a correction-only update.
objectives: Identify which details about the requested source correction are established and which remain UNKNOWN.
Explain why the existing module and its source metadata are required before affected instructional material can be corrected.
Determine what evidence would permit a correction while preserving unaffected material.

sections.title: Declared scope and level
paragraphs: This is an intermediate-level treatment of the evidence boundary surrounding the requested correction. It assumes only that the learner can read a JSON object containing named fields and arrays.

The meaning of memory boundaries in the existing learning content is UNKNOWN. The supplied material does not establish whether the term concerns agent context, persistent memory, data retention, authorization, process isolation, or another subject, so this module does not assert a topical definition.

sections.title: Source change status
paragraphs: The cited topical source that moved or exceeded its review cadence is UNKNOWN. The only supplied citation inventory entry is the local path content/modules/reliable-agent-workflows/memory-boundaries.json, described as having an unregistered publisher and never having been verified. No prior topical source title, HTTPS URL, verification date, or replacement location was supplied.

The instructional material affected by the source change is therefore UNKNOWN. Identifying that effect requires the existing sources array, the previous source location or review metadata, and the sections whose claims depend on that source. No topical correction is asserted without that evidence.
sections.callout: UNKNOWN information is omitted rather than converted into an unsupported claim.

sections.title: Preserving reviewed material
paragraphs: A correction-only update requires the verbatim existing module as its baseline. Comparing the corrected file with that baseline is what reveals whether unrelated wording, identifiers, questions, metadata, or citations changed.

The existing module was not supplied, so its unaffected material cannot be reproduced or certified as unchanged. The baseline file and preferably its repository revision are required before a minimal correction can preserve review history.

sections.title: Evidence needed to complete the correction
paragraphs: To establish that a source moved, the correction needs the prior source URL and an authoritative replacement page or redirect. To establish that review cadence elapsed, it needs the prior verification date, the review cadence, and the date of a direct source check.

To establish the correction's instructional effect, the reviewer also needs the existing sections, knowledge-check questions, and source entries. With that evidence, the reviewer can change the obsolete citation and only the claims or answers that the authoritative source change actually affects.

sections.title: JSON delivery boundary
paragraphs: The delivery format is one JSON object. JSON defines objects as collections of name and value members, and a parser expects the input to follow JSON grammar. Commentary or formatting outside the serialized object can prevent the file from being parsed as the required single value.

Placing sources as the final serialized member satisfies the requested presentation order. JSON object member order is not a portable semantic guarantee, so this placement should not be interpreted as a general ordering rule for JSON data.

questions.prompt: Which cited topical source does the supplied material establish as having moved or exceeded its review cadence?
choices: No cited topical source is established; its identity is UNKNOWN.
The JSON standard is established as the moved topical source.
A named provider document is established as overdue.
questions.explanation: The module states that no prior topical source title, HTTPS URL, verification date, or replacement location was supplied. The identity of the source requiring the topical correction is therefore UNKNOWN.

questions.prompt: What is required before unaffected material can be certified as unchanged?
choices: A newly written replacement module without reference to the prior file
The verbatim existing module as a baseline for comparison
A guessed definition of memory boundaries
questions.explanation: The existing module is the baseline needed to compare changes and determine whether unrelated content, identifiers, questions, metadata, or citations were altered.

questions.prompt: What does this module conclude about the instructional material affected by the unidentified source change?
choices: The affected material is UNKNOWN until the existing source dependencies are available.
questions.explanation: Without the existing source list and the claims that depend on it, the affected instructional material cannot be identified responsibly.
